purpose: Small synthetic-only sensitivity audit of the two fixed 100-update GT-supervised STE-FlowNet diagnostic checkpoints; not a formal model comparison or checkpoint-selection run.

data.split: all fixed validation rollouts, no filtering
data.labels: shared 30ms endpoint flow and shared visibility-valid mask

models.inference: ordinary model.eval(), event representation only; no GT input

input_conditions.normal: Original registered five-bin per-polarity event representation.
input_conditions.zero_events: Set the complete event tensor to zero while retaining the original normal-input common mask.
input_conditions.reverse_bins: Reverse the five temporal-bin order independently for each polarity; preserves each pixel's per-polarity total and the normal event spatial support, but changes temporal ordering. This is a representation perturbation, not a reconstruction of reversed raw events.

fixed_regions.common_event_active: Union of nonzero spatial support from both original normal generator inputs, intersected with shared GT validity; frozen before any intervention and identical for both arms and all conditions.
fixed_regions.active_motion: Fixed common_event_active intersected with GT magnitude >= 0.5 pixels per 30ms endpoint interval.

metrics: EPE on full_valid, common_event_active, and active_motion
zero-flow EPE on the same unchanged masks
prediction magnitude and direction cosine on active_motion
input hash, nonzero support, and aggregate representation count
interpretation_limits: A response to perturbation shows input sensitivity only; it does not establish correct event-to-motion learning.
The checkpoints were trained with synthetic GT supervision for 100 updates; this does not validate the formal self-supervised objective.
The two held-out rollouts belong to one registered validation layout family and have sparse shared event support on the vertical path.
